DRAG DROP -
Refer to the exhibit. An engineer must provision a VXLAN deployment. The OSPF has already been configured as the underlay protocol. All BGP configurations will be performed using the template method. The deployment must meet these requirements: the local update source for leaf switches must be loopback1; the router ID must be the local loopback IP address; and the external BGP connections must use a template name. Drag and drop the configuration snippets from the bottom to complete the configuration.
context: Topology: a leaf switch with Lo0 - 10.255.255.1 and Lo1 - 10.255.255.10, running BGP and OSPF.
imageNote: Diagram: a leaf switch with Lo0 (10.255.255.1) at top and Lo1 (10.255.255.10) at bottom, with BGP running over an inner OSPF underlay.
theory: To scale EVPN leaf-to-spine BGP configuration, NX-OS lets you define a reusable template peer that bundles common session parameters — remote-as, update-source, BFD, timers, and address-family activation — once, and then apply it to individual neighbor statements with inherit peer instead of repeating every parameter under each neighbor. The BGP router-id and update-source both point to the same stable loopback used to establish the EVPN overlay session, while the actual VXLAN MAC/IP reachability information is carried specifically under address-family l2vpn evpn, the address family that both activates EVPN route exchange and applies send-community extended, needed for route-target-based VRF/VNI import and export. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 3 — VXLAN EVPN BGP Peer Templates)
